note: Counterfactuals vary ONE user-controlled input at a time, re-score through the REAL handler, and re-classify the affected sentence. Every varied input is something a user can legitimately change (profile content or matching preferences); system-assigned fields (orgId) and derived artifacts (embedding vectors) are never edited directly.

cases.permittedInput: Profile editor: the user edits their interest list.
cases.note: User-controlled interests no longer overlap; the interest sentence must lose its feature support.

cases.permittedInput: Profile editor: the user updates their experience level.
cases.note: Experience moved to the mentor's own level (gap 0 -> 0.7); the ideal-gap sentence must lose support.

cases.permittedInput: Profile editor: the user changes their professional field from Software to Design; the platform then recomputes the profile embedding from profile content.
cases.variedInput: scoringData.profile.field, with the embedding recomputed via deriveEmbedding (the synthetic embedder standing in for the production embedding model)
cases.note: The embedding vector is NEVER edited directly: only the user-controlled profile field changes, and the embedder recomputes the vector from it, exactly as the production pipeline would. Cosine similarity with the mentor drops from ~0.99 to ~0.32, below the 0.8 threshold; the semantic-similarity sentence must lose support.

cases.permittedInput: Match-settings editor: the user changes the role they are seeking from mentee to mentor.
cases.note: With both sides seeking the mentor role the roles are same-role (0.7), no longer complementary (1.0); the complementary-roles sentence must lose support.

cases.permittedInput: Match-settings editor: the user changes their organization matching preference. orgId itself is system-assigned and is never varied here.
cases.note: The mentee's org matching preference changes from same_org to different_org. With constraint strings no longer identical the short-circuit is gone and the differing orgs resolve to orgConstraintMatch 0.0; the same-organization sentence must become a false reason.
cases.sentence: You are in the same organization as this match.
